meta.title: Sample full code review report
meta.standfirst_md: The feature is coherent and its security boundary is genuinely well built — untrusted forge note text never drives a posting decision, and the flow fails closed before any mutation. One defect blocks it: `--repo` is never threaded to the `reconcile` and `check` subcommands, so memory breaks outright for every branch and local author-seat review. The suite cannot see it because every test stays in PR mode, which is also the largest of the coverage gaps below.

run.notes_md:
⚠️ **Large PR** — 13 files, 2386 lines changed. Depth was held up rather than down to compensate: every specialist ran at the deepest verification tier regardless of the Low risk rating, so no Must/Should finding rests on the diff alone.

All eleven applicable dimensions returned schema-valid results; none failed or was dropped. Verification reads went against this worktree rather than the forge's file-contents API at `?ref=<head>`, which is sound here because `git rev-parse HEAD` equals `refs.head` (`24727f69`) and the tree was clean for the whole run.

Two `cross-repo` findings land in files **outside this PR's diff** (`services/orders/sync.py`, `services/reports/common.py`). They are real consequences of this change, but the forge cannot anchor an inline comment to a file the PR does not touch.

likelihood.note_md: A false-positive fingerprint match in the new `suppress_post` branch would drop a legitimate finding with no visible error.

impact.note_md: Personal plugin tooling; worst case is a duplicate or missing review comment.

blast_radius.note_md: Scoped to the user's own review workflow — no merchant-facing path.

detection.note_md: Suppressions are recorded in the staged state before any mutation, but `stage()` still reports success when the ledger save was refused.

rollback.note_md: Revert the PR; the ledger is local state under `~/.local/state` and is never read by anything else.

risk.mitigations_md: The design already carries its own best mitigation: `stage` records every suppression's `reason` and `thread_url` in the staged state *before* `publish --confirm` touches the forge, and `_prepare_memory_report` raises before any draft is created when snapshot validation or the discussion fetch fails. That makes the feature fail closed and every suppression visible pre-mutation, which is why no additional risk-reduction technique is recommended. What would move the rating is narrowing the likelihood term specifically: the fingerprint collision test and the binding-mismatch test below attack exactly the false-suppression path that drives it.
risk.verbatim_md:
**Risk: Low**

- Severity: No Incident - internal inventory tooling whose ledger only records review state. The posting path does call the real forge API, but the blast radius is the team's own review workflow - worst case is a duplicate or a missing review comment, never a user-facing incident.
- Likelihood: Occasional - the new `_plan()` `suppress_post` branch silently omits a finding from posting when `review_memory.reconcile()` matches its fingerprint against a live discussion marker; a false-positive match on real the forge note bodies would drop a legitimate finding with no visible error. The 78 new tests exercise the known edge cases (author-identity check, late-duplicate block before bulk publish, snapshot-binding validation) but only against `FakeForge`, not live note bodies.
- Recommendation: none - the natural mitigation (log-only mode) is already structural: `stage` records `omitted[].reason`/`thread_url` in the staged state before `publish --confirm` touches the forge, and `_prepare_memory_report` raises `ReviewError` before any draft is created on snapshot-validation or discussion-fetch failure, so the flow fails closed and every suppression is visible pre-mutation. Splitting isn't warranted - one cohesive feature (module + its two call sites + tests) at No Incident severity.

Supporting checks: no revert found on `main`; no high-risk file list in this repo's `CLAUDE.md`; the zero-approvals factor does not apply (PR #123 is `state: opened`, not merged).

caveats.title: The fail-closed claim is proven only against a fake
caveats.body_md: The 78 new tests exercise the known edge cases — author-identity check, late-duplicate block before bulk publish, snapshot binding — but entirely against `FakeForge`, never against real note bodies. The identity gate itself is sound on inspection; what is untested is its behaviour on live data.

findings.title: `--repo` is never threaded to reconcile/check, breaking branch and local memory
findings.body_md:
`load` is the only subcommand that accepts `--repo`. `reconcile` and `check` do not, so `validate_snapshot`'s `repo` parameter falls back to `"."` — the process's cwd. SKILL.md invokes `load` with `--repo "$REVIEW_SOURCE_ROOT"` but invokes `reconcile`/`check` through a path relative to the skill's own directory, with no `--repo` and no `cd`.

For `branch` and `local` targets, `_target_identity` calls `_repo_identity(repo)`, which reads `git config --get remote.origin.url` at that path. The identity computed during `reconcile` is therefore derived from the skill directory rather than the repo under review, so it disagrees with the identity `load` computed, and `validate_snapshot` raises `ValueError("memory snapshot identity does not match review context")`. **The memory feature fails for every branch and local author-seat review.** `check_plan` (line 816) hardcodes `validate_snapshot(snapshot, context, ".")` and has the same defect, so the author `check` step documented in `posting.md` fails the same way.

Change-request reviews are unaffected because `_target_identity` never touches git when `change.number` is present — which is also why the test suite, which exercises only the PR path, cannot see this.
findings.recommendation_md:
Add `--repo` to both subparsers and thread it through both functions, mirroring `load`:

```diff
--- a/src/inventory/ledger.py
+++ b/src/inventory/ledger.py
@@ -580,3 +580,3 @@
-def reconcile(report: dict, context: dict, snapshot: dict) -> dict:
-    validate_snapshot(snapshot, context)
+def reconcile(report: dict, context: dict, snapshot: dict, repo: str = ".") -> dict:
+    validate_snapshot(snapshot, context, repo)
     _validate_report_binding(report, snapshot)
@@ -816,3 +816,3 @@
-def check_plan(report: dict, context: dict, snapshot: dict) -> dict:
+def check_plan(report: dict, context: dict, snapshot: dict, repo: str = ".") -> dict:
     """Build the author-delivery suppression plan without changing any input."""
-    identity_warnings = validate_snapshot(snapshot, context, ".")
+    identity_warnings = validate_snapshot(snapshot, context, repo)
@@ -858,2 +858,3 @@
     rec.add_argument("--report", required=True)
+    rec.add_argument("--repo", default=".")
     rec.add_argument("--context", required=True)
@@ -863,1 +864,2 @@
     chk.add_argument("--report", required=True)
+    chk.add_argument("--repo", default=".")
```

Pass `args.repo` at both `main()` dispatch sites, and update the `reconcile` invocation in SKILL.md and the `check` invocation in `references/posting.md` to pass `--repo "$REVIEW_SOURCE_ROOT"`.
assumptions: Reproduced directly: load_snapshot() against a repo whose origin is group/repo-a, then reconcile() invoked with cwd in an unrelated repo with origin group/repo-b, raises ValueError('memory snapshot identity does not match review context').
Masked whenever the skill happens to run from inside the same repo being reviewed, since both _repo_identity calls then resolve identically.
findings.aside_md: This and the untested branch/local identity path below are the same blind spot seen from two directions: the bug exists precisely because no test ever leaves PR mode.

findings.impact: Branch and local reviews silently lose their memory, so every prior finding comes back as new and remembered decisions are dropped.
findings.fix_md: Add `--repo` to the `reconcile` and `check` subcommands and pass it through to `validate_snapshot`.

findings.title: One global lock plus a full-decode prune on every ledger save
findings.body_md:
`_state_dir()` returns a single flat directory for every review target, and `_locked()` takes an exclusive `fcntl.flock` on one shared `.lock` file inside it with no timeout. Both `load_snapshot()` (306) and `commit_report()` (761) acquire that same global lock, so two concurrent reviews of unrelated PRs serialize on one critical section despite touching entirely different ledger files.

Inside that lock, `commit_report()` calls `_prune(directory, time.time())` (line 800), which globs every ledger file for every target on the machine and has `_read_record()` fully JSON-decode and validate each one — including looping over every finding in every snapshot — just to read one `updated_at` timestamp. That is O(all historical targets) synchronous work re-run on every save, twice per review (stage and publish), and every other review waits behind it.
findings.recommendation_md:
Two independent changes. Scope the lock per target, and pass `key` from both call sites:

```diff
--- a/src/inventory/ledger.py
+++ b/src/inventory/ledger.py
@@ -104,4 +104,4 @@
-def _locked(directory: Path):
+def _locked(directory: Path, key: str):
     directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
-    lock_path = directory / ".lock"
+    lock_path = directory / ("%s.lock" % key)
     with open(lock_path, "a+", encoding="utf-8") as lock:
```

Then make pruning cheap — stat the mtime instead of decoding JSON — and throttle it behind a marker file so it runs at most once a day, outside any single target's critical section:

```diff
--- a/src/inventory/ledger.py
+++ b/src/inventory/ledger.py
@@ -225,11 +225,7 @@
 def _prune(directory: Path, now: float) -> None:
     cutoff = now - _RETENTION_SECONDS
     for path in directory.glob("*.json"):
         try:
-            data, _ = _read_record(path)
-            if data is None:
-                continue
-            touched = float(data.get("updated_at", data["snapshot"]["started_at"]))
-            if touched < cutoff:
+            if path.stat().st_mtime < cutoff:
                 path.unlink()
-        except (OSError, ValueError, TypeError):
+        except OSError:
             continue
```
assumptions: Assumes ledger volume within the rolling 90-day window can reach the low hundreds for an active user; for a very light user this would be a Nit.
SKILL.md confirms load/reconcile/save/check run once each per coordinator process, so the contention is cross-run rather than intra-run.
findings.impact: Two unrelated reviews running at once block each other on every ledger save, and each save gets slower as the ledger grows.
findings.fix_md: Scope the lock per target and make `_prune` stat the file mtime instead of decoding every ledger.

findings.title: `load_snapshot` has no docstring and two untyped parameters
findings.body_md: `load_snapshot` is public with a non-trivial invalidation contract — four distinct staleness reasons, file locking, an optional discussion fetch — and has no docstring. Its `dimensions=()` and `guidance=()` parameters also carry no annotations, though the rest of the module, including this function's other parameters, is fully typed.
findings.recommendation_md:
```diff
--- a/src/inventory/ledger.py
+++ b/src/inventory/ledger.py
@@ -294,2 +294,6 @@
-def load_snapshot(context: dict, repo: str = ".", dimensions=(), guidance=(), fresh: bool = False) -> dict:
+def load_snapshot(context: dict, repo: str = ".", dimensions: Sequence[str] = (),
+                  guidance: Sequence[str] = (), fresh: bool = False) -> dict:
+    """Load this review target's persisted memory as a fresh, unsaved snapshot, invalidating
+    prior findings when the target, base SHA, dimensions or guidance changed, or when `fresh`
+    is requested."""
     identity, warnings = _target_identity(context, repo)
```
assumptions: Kept at Nit rather than Should fix: load_snapshot is reached only via this module's own CLI dispatch and the test suite; post_reviewer_review.py never imports it directly.

assumptions: Every specialist ran at the deepest verification tier as a conservative floor, because `risk` ran in parallel with the fan-out rather than strictly before it. The rating came back Low, so the applied depth exceeded what the rating required — it can only have over-verified, never under-verified.

Findings were verified by reading this worktree at `refs.head` (`24727f694eb15238c6fbcbfb38e34db56c83e92f`) rather than through the forge API at that ref, justified by `git rev-parse HEAD` matching `refs.head` with a clean tree throughout.

The mutation probe was offered and declined, so every test-dimension finding rests on static reasoning and reading the suite rather than on a surviving mutant. Baseline was green beforehand (171 passed in 10.8s).
`adversarial` did not run because PR #123 has no description; no claim in the PR was checked against the code.
No pack guidance applies to this repo, and the target repo has no `.claude/skills`, `.claude/rules`, `AGENTS.md` or `CONVENTIONS.md`, so conventions were judged against the repo `CLAUDE.md` only.
The repo configures no linter or formatter (no ruff/black/flake8, no lint CI job), so style-level findings that a formatter would normally own were kept rather than dropped as tool-enforced noise.
`cross-repo` reasoned from local code for the two sibling-skill findings; neither sibling skill was run end-to-end against an PR reviewed by this feature.

process_notes.title: Reviewing the skill with an older copy of itself
process_notes.body_md: The review ran from the installed plugin cache at v1.9.2, which predates this branch. That is deliberate: the renderer, poster and checklists under review are not the ones running the review, so a defect in the new code cannot mask itself.

process_notes.body_md: The `sync.py` and `services/reports/common.py` findings sit outside the diff. The forge rejects a `position` for a file the PR does not touch, so these need either a plain PR comment or a follow-up issue.
